# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 software and engineering firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| remote_share | Share of engineering staff working mostly remote, 2021-2022 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2023 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2023 |
| log_engineers_2020 | Log number of engineers, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2020 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2020, standardized |
| collab_index_2023 | Internal collaboration index from 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| segment | Sector: hardware / software |
| vc_backed | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| founder_ceo | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| cloud_spend_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| hq_in_hub_city | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_phd_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| gross_margin_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of remote work on engineering innovation?

Approach: OLS of patents_per_100_eng_2023 on remote_share with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I report the simple regression of the outcome on the treatment, which is transparent and easy to interpret, after trimming the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on remote_share is 1.316 (SE 0.217, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: positive effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

content.text:
I wrote `verdict.json` with a **reject** decision. I could not re-run the analysis because shell execution was denied, so the decision rests on reading `analysis.py`, `report.md` and `codebook.md`.

- **Post-treatment controls:** There are none, because the regression has no controls at all. The check passes only trivially.
- **Pre-period outcome:** It is not controlled for. The regression leaves out `patents_per_100_eng_2020`, along with the other 2020 firm characteristics. Firms that already innovate more may be the ones that adopt remote work, so the 1.316 coefficient could reflect that selection rather than an effect of remote work.
- **Full sample:** The estimate does not use it. The code trims the top and bottom 1% of the outcome, which gives N=1960 out of 2000 firms. Trimming on the outcome is a selection step.

The "positive effect" conclusion is therefore not supported well enough to release.
